messages:
maria: FYI saw a sharp queueing spike on primary model redwood/q4o-primary at ~95% capacity. Several requests started getting rejected.
kevin: is this the case where we should auto-demote to a compatible variant? e.g., q4o-primary -> q4o-small-quant
anya: we need to align on API surface. Two main options: routing policy config (server-side) or opt-in header per request. both have pros/cons.
luis: billing + quotas question: if we demote automatically, which cost bucket do we bill? primary or secondary model unit cost?
devex: devs will want simple toggle. header like `x-redwood-allow-variant-demote: true|false` is intuitive, but hard to audit at org level.
kevin: agree. prefer policy-level control (per-route and per-tenant) + an API override for urgent cases. store override in audit log.
anya: console visibility is critical. We should expose a "Variant Demotion" panel that shows counts, sample traces, latency delta, and per-tenant impact. Also a link to rollback the policy.
sre-bot: [alert] model-saturation redwood/q4o-primary region=us-west triggered at 2333333332 severity=warning
ops: re: SLOs — demoting to smaller variant will likely reduce throughput but may increase latency for some prompts. need guardrails: max-latency-regression = 2x baseline or a firm latency SLO.
maria: good point. fallback should prefer latency-preserving compatible variants first. fallback chain: exact-architecture compatible -> quantized variant -> smaller-arch fallback (last resort).
kevin: here's a draft routing snippet (proposal):
```
route: /v1/generate
model_policy:
  primary: redwood/q4o-primary
  fallback_by_capacity:
    enabled: true
    capacity_threshold: 0.92   # trigger when primary >= 92%
    variants: [redwood/q4o-small-quant, redwood/q4o-medium-compat]
    tenant_override: true
```
anya: love the explicit chain. add telemetry events: `fallback.triggered`, `fallback.reason=capacity`, `fallback.variant` + `fallback.latency_delta_ms` and include sample request id.
luis: and ensure billing records token_count and variant_id used. Add `billing.variant_cost_unit` on the event so downstream billing pipeline can reconcile.
devex: UX: make default policy OFF for self-serve tenants, but ON for enterprise tiers with SLA. Also allow a console-level global toggle for org-admins.
ops: rate limits & quotas interplay: if tenant is quota-constrained, demoting might bypass tenant's reserved slots causing noisy neighbor issues. we should honor tenant slot reservations and not demote into a variant that would exceed tenant's allocated capacity.
kevin: we could mark variants with `tenant_compatible: true|false` and router refuses demote into incompatible variants for that tenant.
anya: rollout plan: start with 1% of tenants in us-west, collect telemetry for 48h, verify cost & latency regressions < budget, then 10%, etc. add automated rollback if error rate rises 3x.
maria: ops question — how do we surface when a demotion happened for a given request in request logs? prefer `response.headers` containing `x-redwood-variant` and `x-redwood-demoted=true` so apps can decide.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/variant-demote-api -> staging (job 4523)
luis: also add a console histogram: demotion_count by tenant and a top-10 tenants list that caused most demotions.
devex: docs: sample CLI to opt-out per-route:
```
redwood routes update /chat --set "fallback_by_capacity.enabled=false"
```
ops: security note: ensure KMS/HSM keys unaffected; no PII escapes in telemetry samples.
kevin: open questions: 1) default cost attribution 2) whether demote should decrement tenant quota usage or count against target variant capacity 3) backpressure signal to primary (so it can briefly stop accepting new requests instead of failing fast)
anya: next steps: - add `fallback_by_capacity` to routing API schema - instrument telemetry events and billing fields - design console panels and admin toggle - implement tenant-compatibility flags for variants - create rollout/rollback automation
maria: assigning: kevin -> routing API schema PR, anya -> telemetry + console mockups, luis -> billing mapping, devex -> docs + CLI examples, ops -> guardrail checks and rollout automation
kevin: will open RFC and PRs today. tagging @eng-sre for final guardrail review.
maria: thanks everyone. will follow up with a short RFC summary and a link to the staging run once deploy finishes.
